correctness.rationale: Exact shape identity after second arrival; strictly decreasing peak multiplier; rigorous three-interval duration monotonicity for all subcritical thresholds; high-threshold classification by pointwise peak bound. The analytic proof establishes precisely two possible maximizing delays and every tie and zero-duration case. An exact rational exponential witness proves strict staggered superiority at threshold one quarter. Standalone standard-library checks pass 1,100 independent crossing comparisons and further grid comparisons but are not substitutes for the global proof.

originality.rationale: Full accessible primary articles and three closest relevant publicly available mathematical manuscripts were compared by what their theorems imply. The gamma/Nash kernel, level crossings, storm timing and general crest-count mathematics are prior art. The inspected texts do not furnish the exact global time-above-threshold optimum over arrival lag, including the two-candidate set and ties. Primary-field models do not empirically validate the equal instantaneous two-reservoir assumptions.

value.rationale: Hydrological exceedance duration is a motivated hazard proxy used in estuarine flood timing research. The theorem is a complete global optimization for the natural two-impulse two-reservoir benchmark. It reveals that synchronization maximizes peak but not necessarily duration, gives only two physically interpretable candidate lags, and certifies a more than 37-percent difference at a natural fractional threshold. Neither a calibrated field claim nor a trivial renaming of the earlier crest-count results is involved.
